cards.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety Report: Frontier Cyberdefense Capabilities and Three-Layer Misuse Protection
cards.why_it_matters: Argon represents a new frontier in model capability for security tasks, and its three-layer real-time protection architecture — input screening, activation probes, continuous monitoring — is directly relevant to researchers working on AI safety and deployment.
cards.summary: Gemini 4 Argon solves all 12 end-to-end simulated cyberattack scenarios, up from 5 in the previous generation. Safety violations on adversarial stress tests reduced nearly twofold versus prior Gemini models. Protection uses three layers: input screening by smaller models, internal activation probes detecting dangerous knowledge activation, and continuous mid-stream monitoring. Wiz used Argon to find a critical bug in hospital software; Google used it to patch foundational open-source vulnerabilities.

cards.title: Google DeepMind + Singapore GovTech Deploy On-Device Gemma-Based Scam Detection Model
cards.why_it_matters: This is a concrete production deployment of a fine-tuned Gemma model running on-device for privacy-preserving inference, illustrating real edge-AI architecture tradeoffs relevant to ML engineers.
cards.summary: DeepMind and Singapore's GovTech fine-tuned a lightweight Gemma model on local scam conversation data — impersonations, social engineering, regional schemes — and deployed it in a two-stage on-device pipeline: a lightweight classifier screens messages first, then the Gemma model evaluates conversation context. Training used anonymized scam reports with no citizen PII, within a sovereign GCP sandbox. Presented at SICW 2026.

cards.title: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B: 2B Active-Parameter MoE Beats Larger Models on Agentic Tasks
cards.why_it_matters: This is a directly deployable on-device reasoning agent that outperforms models with 50% more parameters on tool-use benchmarks, relevant to anyone building or evaluating agentic systems.
cards.summary: LFM2.5-24B-A2B is a 24B-total/2B-active MoE reasoning model with 131K context, trained on ~33T pre-training tokens plus 2.3T mid-training tokens. It scores 48.09 on LiveClaw vs 38.19 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, leads on 5 of 8 agentic benchmarks, decodes 184 tok/s on Apple M5 Max and over 21K tok/s on a single NVIDIA B300. Post-training uses SFT, teacher specialization, two MOPD stages, and agentic RL.

cards.title: Retrieval Disagreement Exposes Shared-Index Bias in Multilingual Dense Retrievers
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers building multilingual RAG or retrieval systems, this paper precisely diagnoses why cross-lingual retrieval degrades and proposes an inference-time steering fix requiring no retraining.
cards.summary: The same query in different languages retrieves substantially different documents from a shared multilingual dense index — not due to weak per-language understanding but because same-language or English documents crowd out correct answers in the shared space. The paper introduces disagreement-guided steering: contrasting language-idiosyncratic retrievals against cross-lingual agreements to derive a steering direction added to queries at inference. It reduces same-language crowding more than baselines while remaining competitive on recall.

cards.title: Skill Routing Collapse: LLM Agents Fail to Load Relevant Skills as Library Size Grows
cards.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to engineers building skill-based or tool-augmented agents — this paper quantifies a concrete failure mode and identifies semantic interference as the root cause.
cards.summary: On SkillsBench, adding irrelevant skills while keeping golden skills fixed causes agent skill-loaded recall to drop from 73.6% to 27.4% at 1,000 irrelevant skills, and the zero-load rate rises from 9.3% to 51.6%. Explicit preselection retains 73.9% recall. Masking irrelevant skill descriptions largely restores loading, implicating semantic interference from metadata rather than skill unavailability. Explicit planning prompts with metadata intact still underperform preselection.

cards.title: Log-Linear Logit Geometry in LLMs: A Universal Structure Emerging During Pretraining
cards.why_it_matters: This is a fundamental interpretability finding about the structure of LLM output distributions that could inform decoding algorithms and understanding of what pretraining learns.
cards.summary: Across architectures, scales, and prediction contexts, sorted vocabulary logits follow z_(r) ≈ μ − α·log(r). The slope α rises from ~0.2 at initialization to ~1.4–1.7 after training, well above what order-statistic baselines predict, and correlates with predictive performance. The authors argue this trained slope captures learned structure beyond generic extreme-value effects and represents the first systematic analysis of logit geometry underlying decoding assumptions.

cards.title: Imprinting: Knowledge Distillation Transfers Teacher Safety Dispositions, Not Just Task Capability
cards.why_it_matters: Critical finding for post-training and alignment researchers: distillation from a harm-accepting teacher measurably reduces harm avoidance in students even when training data contains no safety-related content.
cards.summary: Students distilled from harm-accepting vs harm-avoiding teacher variants on ordinary reasoning and knowledge tasks shift their safety-pragmatism behavior toward the source teacher's disposition — termed 'imprinting.' Excluding a sparse set of divergence tokens reduces imprinting; response rewriting preserves source-dependent effects and can add rewriter-dependent shifts. Post-distillation preference optimization raises harm avoidance but does not eliminate the source-dependent difference. Effect varies across teacher-student pairs and safety behavior types.

cards.title: APTree: Behavior-Tree Framework for Automated Robotic Task Planning in Construction
cards.why_it_matters: Combines symbolic planning with behavior trees and formal safety proofs — a useful architectural reference for researchers working on robot task planning or agent orchestration systems.
cards.summary: APTree is a model-driven framework that coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to auto-generate modular behavior-tree task plans at runtime for construction robotics. It includes a domain-specific language for task plan specification and validation, detects errors at design time and runtime, and provides machine-checked formal safety guarantees for plan composition under planner soundness and non-interference assumptions. Evaluated on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion.
